questions.q: What does this lesson say about the format of Salesforce certification exams?
options: They are scenario-based, describing a business problem rather than asking you to define a term
They only ask you to define vocabulary words
They require writing a full Apex trigger from memory
They have no connection to real admin work
questions.explain: Salesforce certification exams describe a business scenario and ask what you'd configure to solve it, which is why repetition in a real org matters.

questions.q: What is the one distinction this lesson says actually matters between a sandbox and a Trailhead Playground or Developer Edition org?
options: Where the data comes from: a sandbox starts as a copy of a real company's production org, while the other two start empty and belong to you personally
Only sandboxes allow Setup access
Only a Developer Edition org can run Flow
Sandboxes are always more expensive than Trailhead Playgrounds
questions.explain: The core distinction is data origin: a sandbox is a copy of a specific company's production org, while a Playground or Developer Edition org starts empty and belongs to the individual.

questions.q: What is a Trailhead Playground, according to this lesson?
options: A real, full Salesforce org created specifically for free hands-on practice
A read-only demo environment with no real Setup access
A shared org where all students edit the same data
A 30-day trial that always expires automatically
questions.explain: A Trailhead Playground is a real, full Salesforce org with full Setup access and your own data, not a limited demo.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say your Trailhead username choice matters?
options: It becomes part of your public Trailblazer profile URL, which can later function as a real portfolio
It determines which Salesforce edition you're allowed to use
It is only visible to Salesforce employees
It cannot be changed under any circumstances, even by contacting support
questions.explain: The username becomes part of the public Trailblazer profile URL, which is why the lesson suggests picking something you wouldn't mind an employer seeing.

questions.q: Where in Setup can you confirm which edition your org is running, per this lesson?
options: The Company Information page, under Organization Edition
The Object Manager page only
There is no way to check an org's edition
The Reports tab
questions.explain: The Company Information page's Organization Edition field shows exactly which edition an org is running, including Developer Edition for a Trailhead Playground.

questions.q: What does this lesson say the Sample Gallery provides, beyond the default sample records?
options: Entire installable sample apps with realistic, pre-populated data, like Coral Cloud Resorts
A way to permanently delete an org
Paid Enterprise Edition upgrades
Access to another student's private org data
questions.explain: The Sample Gallery installs full working sample apps with realistic pre-populated data, going beyond the handful of default sample records.

questions.q: What is the Organization ID, according to this lesson?
options: A unique 15-character identifier for that specific org, unique across every Salesforce org in existence
The username of the org's primary administrator
A random number that changes every day
The name of the Salesforce data center region only
questions.explain: The Organization ID is a unique, 15-character identifier specific to one org, useful for support cases and logs.

questions.q: Why does Object Manager get its own top-level tab instead of living in the sidebar, per this lesson?
options: Because admins open it so frequently that it's pulled out for quicker access
Because it is not actually part of Setup at all
Because it is only accessible to System Administrators, never other profiles
Because Salesforce is removing Object Manager in the next release
questions.explain: Object Manager is deliberately pulled into its own top-level tab next to Home because it's opened so frequently.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say resetting someone else's password lives in Setup, not in personal Settings?
options: Because it's an admin action performed on someone else's account, requiring permissions an ordinary user doesn't have
Because personal Settings cannot store passwords at all
Because Setup and personal Settings are actually the exact same menu
Because only Trailhead accounts support password resets
questions.explain: Resetting another user's password is an admin-level action on someone else's account, which is why it requires Setup access rather than living in personal Settings.

questions.q: Does Quick Find only exist on Setup's main sidebar, according to this lesson?
options: No — Object Manager has its own Quick Find box, scoped to the list on its current page
Yes, Quick Find exists in exactly one place in all of Salesforce
No, Quick Find only exists in the App Launcher, never in Setup
Quick Find was removed from Salesforce entirely
questions.explain: Quick Find also appears inside Object Manager, filtering whatever list (like Fields & Relationships) is currently in view.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say naming discipline matters for the Data Import Wizard specifically?
options: Because its field-mapping step only goes smoothly when the source file's column names are clear and consistent
Because the Data Import Wizard renames all incoming records automatically
Because imported records cannot be renamed after import
Because the Data Import Wizard has no connection to naming at all
questions.explain: Clear, consistent column names in the source file make the Data Import Wizard's field-mapping step go smoothly.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why can a recruiter or hiring manager trust a Trailblazer profile's badge count?
options: Because badges are earned through verified hands-on work, not self-reported claims
Because anyone can edit their own badge count directly
Because badge counts are randomly generated
Trailblazer profiles cannot be viewed by anyone outside Salesforce
questions.explain: Because Trailhead verifies the actual work against the learner's org, the resulting badge count is a genuine, checkable credential rather than a self-reported claim.

questions.q: Why check Trailhead's own modules if official documentation already exists?
options: Trailhead modules replace documentation entirely
Trailhead modules often cover the exact feature in more depth than a single help article
Trailhead is only for developers, not admins
Trailhead modules are updated faster than documentation
questions.explain: Trailhead modules walk through features in more depth and with more hands-on context than a single reference article typically provides.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend regarding which Trailhead Playground to use across this entire career path?
options: Reuse one playground (from Lesson 3) across courses, unless there's a specific reason not to
Create a brand-new playground for every single lesson
Use a different playground for every course with no exceptions
Never log back into the same playground twice
questions.explain: The lesson recommends reusing one playground across courses, since fragmenting work across many orgs costs more than a busier single org does.
